headline: Regional Touring and Wind Energy Interpretive Access
reservation: While the scenic drive itself is a public highway system, specific attractions like the Wind Energy Interpretive Centre or provincial park campgrounds along the route require separate admissions. Confirm seasonal hours for museums and local heritage sites via the official PEI tourism portal.

days.title: Red Sands and Wind Power

stops.name: North Cape Lighthouse
stops.detail: Observe the meeting of the Gulf of St. Lawrence and the Northumberland Strait near the reef.

stops.name: Wind Energy Interpretive Centre
stops.detail: Learn about the significant wind farm operations at the northernmost tip of the island.

days.driving: Allow 2 to 3 hours; the winding coastal roads invite frequent stops.
days.note: The reef at North Cape is dangerous at high tide; stay behind marked safety barriers.

days.title: Acadian Culture and Artisans

stops.name: St. Simon & St. Jude Church
stops.detail: Visit this historic brick cathedral known for its massive pipe organ and Acadian architecture.

stops.name: Canadian Potato Museum
stops.detail: Explore the agricultural history of O'Leary and the significance of the potato industry to PEI.

days.driving: Allow 1 to 2 hours between rural communities; conditions vary by season.
days.note: Local museums often have shorter hours in the shoulder seasons of June and September.

days.title: Cedar Dunes and Coastal Cliffs

stops.name: Cedar Dunes Provincial Park
stops.detail: Walk the beaches near West Point and view the distinct black-and-white striped lighthouse.

stops.name: Elephant Rock (Coastal Formations)
stops.detail: Observe the rapidly changing sandstone cliffs, noting the impact of erosion on the landscape.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 to 2.5 hours; heavy agricultural machinery may share the road.
days.note: Sandstone structures are fragile; avoid climbing on cliffsides due to instability.

intel.title: Trailhead and Viewpoint Space
intel.text: Parking is generally available at North Cape and West Point, though lots are smaller at community museums. Expect gravel surfaces in rural pull-offs along the western shore.

intel.title: Western Island Coverage
intel.text: Cellular service is reliable in towns like Summerside and Alberton but can be intermittent near the North Cape reef. Download offline maps for navigation through the interior 'Up West' backroads.

intel.title: Gateway Service Stations
intel.text: Fill up in Summerside or O'Leary before venturing to the remote northern tips of the drive. Many rural stations operate on limited evening hours compared to urban centers.

intel.title: Seasonal Operation
intel.text: Many coastal attractions only operate from late June through Labor Day. Visiting in May or October may result in exterior-only viewing of historic sites.

intel.title: Road Conditions
intel.text: The route consists of well-maintained provincial highways, though coastal spray can affect visibility. Watch for cyclists as the Confederation Trail intersects several points on this drive.

plan.arrival: Pick up a rental at Charlottetown Airport (YYG) and drive west to Summerside for supplies and a route briefing.
plan.vehicle: Compact cars are efficient for the loop; RVs are welcome but should stick to primary secondary highways.
plan.goldenHour: West Point Lighthouse is the premier spot for sunset views over the Northumberland Strait.
